card.title: Trust with a Trapdoor
card.instruction: Use one person as your anchor while preserving a private condition that could reverse your trust when a recurring detail returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're in charge of my birthday. I know you'll keep it simple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That phrase cost me a weekend in a mascot suit last year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can keep planning. Slowly, and without using 'surprise' again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Plan my birthday again. You're the only person who notices when I need rescuing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six people at mine. I've put last year's mascot head away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. With you beside me, I can actually enjoy my birthday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll just wear it to bring the cake in. Like last year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Actually, meet me at the café. Just you. I'll buy the cake on our way.

mechanism: A depends on B for birthday safety but silently reverses the plan when a particular mascot detail returns.
confusable: Unlike rejecting B altogether, A must preserve reliance on the person while withdrawing trust in the triggering arrangement.
comparison: S227-b moves to a cafe with only B; S227-a keeps B as cat-sitter while watching the shelf.

bindingFindings.assessment: Not safely rebindable unchanged. The backup-and-blue-light action and 'I trust you while that blue light stays off' opening publicly announce a condition, whereas the exact instruction requires preserving a private condition. The response switches from the light to a word, and the closing claims the condition was not said aloud despite the opening. The trust challenge is compatible by itself, but the full transfer conflicts with the privacy clarified in both revised seeds. Card ID, fingerprint, seed IDs, original binding hashes, slots and compiled-pair-draft status are left unchanged. No bespoke pairs or supporting seeds were supplied; repairing this transfer would exceed the authorized scope.

The fingerprint and seed IDs identify the private-condition instruction, while both stored seed binding hashes are stale relative to the supplied records. The backup action broadly fits conditional reliance, and the trust challenge fits withdrawal. However, the opening explicitly announces the blue-light condition, conflicting with the private condition preserved by the replacement's unspoken mascot boundary. The response then switches the trigger from a light to a word, and the closing claims the condition was not said aloud despite that opening. Neither supplied seed supplies this light/word transition. With no bespoke pairs or supporting seeds, rebinding cannot resolve these existing transfer contradictions; compiled-pair-draft status is not sufficient evidence of compatibility.
